info.name: Bus Ticketing API
info.description:
# Bus Ticketing API

**1 bus · 40 seats · one ticket per seat**

## Quick-start
1. Make sure the backend is running (`npm run dev` in the `backend/` folder).
2. Set the `base_url` collection variable to `http://localhost:3000` (or your EC2 public IP).
3. Set `admin_secret` to the value of `ADMIN_SECRET` in your `.env` file.
4. Run **Seed / Health Check** first to confirm the server is live.
5. Work through the folders in order: **Tickets → Admin**.

## Variable reference
| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `base_url` | `http://localhost:3000` | Server root |
| `admin_secret` | `vicky7512` | Required by the reset endpoint |
| `ticket_id` | `5` | Seat ID used in single-ticket requests |

## Response envelope
Every response follows the same shape:
```json
{ "success": true, "data": { ... }, "message": "..." }
```
On error `success` is `false` and `data` is `null`. In development mode a `detail` field with the raw database message is also included.

request.description:
## Health Check

Call this first to confirm the server is up and connected to PostgreSQL.

**Expected:** `200 OK` with `message: "Server is healthy"`.

If you get a connection error, check:
- `npm run dev` is running in the `backend/` folder
- `.env` has the correct `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_NAME`

item.name: Tickets
item.description:
All ticket-related endpoints.

The PATCH endpoint handles three distinct operations depending on what you send:
- **Book** — `status: closed` + passenger fields (creates a reservation)
- **Update** — `status: closed` + changed passenger fields (edits an existing reservation)
- **Cancel** — `status: open` only (frees the seat)

request.description:
## GET /api/tickets

Returns all **40 tickets** ordered by `seat_number` ascending.

Each ticket includes:
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | Primary key |
| `seat_number` | integer | 1 – 40 |
| `status` | string | `open` or `closed` |
| `first_name` | string \| null | Null when open |
| `last_name` | string \| null | Null when open |
| `email` | string \| null | Null when open |
| `gender` | string \| null | `male` or `female`, null when open |
| `booked_at` | timestamp \| null | Set on first booking only |
| `created_at` | timestamp | Row creation time |
| `updated_at` | timestamp | Last update time |

**Used by the frontend:** Yes — `ReservePage` and `DashboardPage` both call this on mount and after every mutation.

request.description:
## GET /api/tickets/open

Returns only seats with `status = 'open'` — i.e. seats available for booking.

**When to use:** Use this instead of `GET /tickets` when you only need to show available seats and don't want to send booked-seat data over the network (better for large buses or slower connections).

**Used by the frontend:** No — the frontend calls `GET /tickets` and filters client-side. This endpoint is ready to use if you switch to server-side filtering.

request.description:
## GET /api/tickets/closed

Returns only seats with `status = 'closed'` — i.e. all booked seats with passenger details.

**When to use:** Use this for a passenger manifest or a report of all bookings without fetching the empty seats too.

**Used by the frontend:** No — the frontend calls `GET /tickets` and filters to `status === 'closed'` in `DashboardPage`. Could be switched to this endpoint to reduce payload size.

## GET /api/tickets/:id

Fetches a single ticket by its **database ID** (not seat number).

> **Tip:** The `id` and `seat_number` are not the same. Seat #5 typically has `id = 5` after a fresh seed, but if rows were deleted and re-inserted the IDs may differ. Always use the `id` returned by `GET /tickets`.

**Used by the frontend:** No — the frontend works from the full cached list and never needs a single-ticket fetch.

**Useful for:** A kiosk or mobile app that stores the ticket ID and needs to refresh just that one seat's state.

request.description:
## GET /api/tickets/:id/owner

Returns only the **passenger details** of a booked seat — no internal DB fields like `created_at` or `updated_at`.

Returns `404` if the seat is open (no owner).

**Used by the frontend:** No — passenger details are already in the full list. Useful for a targeted lookup, e.g. a conductor's app scanning a ticket QR code that contains only the ticket ID.

response.name: 404 — Seat is open (no owner)

item.name: PATCH Book a Ticket — Male (open → closed)

request.description:
## PATCH /api/tickets/:id — Book (open → closed)

Books an **open** seat for a male passenger.

### Required fields
| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | Must be `"closed"` |
| `first_name` | string | Min 1 char |
| `last_name` | string | Min 1 char |
| `email` | string | Valid email format |
| `gender` | string | `"male"` or `"female"` |

### What happens
1. `status` is set to `closed`
2. Passenger fields are saved
3. `booked_at` is stamped to **now** (only on first booking — not overwritten on edits)
4. Event `ticket:booked` is emitted → logged to console and `logs/combined.log`

### On the seat map
Seat turns **blue** (male passenger).

### Error cases
- `400` if any required field is missing
- `400` if the seat is already booked (call Cancel first)

response.name: 400 — Missing required fields

item.name: PATCH Book a Ticket — Female (open → closed)

request.description:
## PATCH /api/tickets/:id — Book (open → closed) for Female

Same endpoint as the male booking — only `gender` differs.

### On the seat map
Seat turns **pink** (female passenger).

> **Tip:** Change `ticket_id` in the collection variables to target a different seat (e.g. `8` for seat #8).

## PATCH /api/tickets/:id — Update passenger details (closed → closed)

Edits the passenger details of an **already booked** seat without cancelling and re-booking.

### Key behaviour
- `status` must still be `"closed"` even though the seat is already closed
- All passenger fields must be sent (even unchanged ones)
- `booked_at` is **not** overwritten — the original booking timestamp is preserved
- No event is emitted for detail-only edits (only for open↔closed transitions)

### Used by the frontend
Yes — the Dashboard **Edit** button calls this via `useUpdatePassenger` → `PATCH /tickets/:id`.

## PATCH /api/tickets/:id — Cancel (closed → open)

Frees a booked seat. All passenger fields (`first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `gender`, `booked_at`) are set to `NULL` automatically by the server — you only need to send `status: open`.

### What happens
1. `status` → `open`
2. All passenger fields → `NULL`
3. `booked_at` → `NULL`
4. Event `ticket:cancelled` is emitted → logged to console and `logs/combined.log`

### On the seat map
Seat turns **green** (available).

### Used by the frontend
Yes — the Dashboard **Delete** button calls this via `useCancelTicket` → `PATCH /tickets/:id` with `{ status: 'open' }`.

### Error case
- `400` if the seat is already open

response.name: 200 — Cancelled successfully
response.body:
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "id": 5,
    "seat_number": 5,
    "status": "open",
    "first_name": null,
    "last_name": null,
    "email": null,
    "gender": null,
    "booked_at": null,
    "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "updated_at": "2024-06-10T11:00:00.000Z"
  },
  "message": "Ticket cancelled successfully"
}

item.name: Admin
item.description:
Admin-only endpoints. Protected by the `ADMIN_SECRET` value from your `.env` file.

> **Never expose the admin secret in client-side code.** These requests should only be made from Postman or a trusted server-side process.

request.description:
## POST /api/admin/reset

Resets **all 40 tickets** to open status in a single operation. Clears every passenger record.

### Authentication
Send `secret` in the request body matching `ADMIN_SECRET` in your `.env`.

### What happens
1. All 40 rows: `status → open`, all passenger fields → `NULL`
2. Event `admin:reset` is emitted → logged to console and `logs/combined.log`

### When to use
- Between trips (bus departs, next journey begins)
- During development/testing to clear test bookings quickly
- As a scheduled nightly job via a cron script

### Used by the frontend
No — currently Postman-only. The frontend has no admin UI. To add one: call `POST /api/admin/reset` from a secured admin page, prompt for the secret, and call `useResetTickets` mutation.

### Error cases
- `401` if `secret` is missing or wrong

> **Warning:** This deletes all passenger data permanently. There is no undo.

response.name: 200 — All tickets reset
